newsitem.title: MACAU: Air Macau raises 1996 passenger growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: Air Macau raises 1996 passenger growth forecast.

text.p: Air Macau said on Monday it expected to carry about 650,000 passengers this year, an increase of about 30 percent over previous forecasts.

"The bookings that we have until the end of the year, as well as the flow of passengers that we have had, allow us to say that we will have about 650,000 passengers until the end of the year," Leonel Miranda, Air Macau executive committee president, said by telephone.
Miranda also said the airline would add two Airbus Industries A321 planes by April 1997.
Air Macau, the flagship carrier of Portugese-run Macau, currently operates two Airbus A320s and two A321s.

Air Macau operates scheduled flights to Taipei, Kaohsiung, Beijing, Shanghai, Xiamen and Bangkok. Miranda said the airline next year planned to extend its network of regular flights to include Hainan Island, Qingdao and Wuhan in China,
By 1999, the year Macau reverts to Chinese rule, Air Macau hoped to fly to 22 destinations, including Australia, he said.
Air Macau began scheduled services on November 9.
